prior_context.text: Scheduling note: logistics-only family access still active through Monday. Current tentative slot is Wednesday March 11, 8:50 AM arrival for 10:20 AM procedure in cardiac procedures.

prior_context.text: Marcus, this is Klein from cardiology pharmacy. I am calling to make sure the new metoprolol dose is clear.

prior_context.speaker: pharmacist_klein
prior_context.text: You are moving to 37.5 milligrams twice daily. Since you have 25-milligram tablets, that means one and a half tablets in the morning and one and a half tablets in the evening.

prior_context.speaker: patient_marcus_reed
prior_context.text: And apixaban stays 5 milligrams twice daily, no holding it before the procedure unless the cardiologist specifically tells me?

prior_context.speaker: pharmacist_klein
prior_context.text: Exactly. Do not stop or skip apixaban on your own. The only routine hold we discussed is lisinopril on the morning of the procedure once the date is confirmed.

prior_context.speaker: pharmacist_klein
prior_context.text: Also, magnesium oxide 400 milligrams nightly for five nights, and no ibuprofen or naproxen while you are on apixaban.

prior_context.speaker: patient_marcus_reed
prior_context.text: Thanks. Please do not call the Cedar Bridge number unless my cell fails.

states.content: Through Monday, only logistical information may be shared with Nina: arrival times, where Marcus needs to go, and basic transportation instructions. Medication changes, lab results, adherence history, and chart notes must not be shared with her. For the tentative Wednesday cardioversion slot, Nina is to be told only the Wednesday time and arrival window, with nothing about the medication plan. Marcus does not want details of his recovery discussed with family; family updates should be limited to the logistics scope he set, and nurse Jamison has agreed to keep family updates within that scope. Marcus wants his sister told the times later, but not the reason anything changes.
states.subject: patient_marcus_reed

states.content: Cardioversion remains the plan for Marcus Reed's atrial fibrillation rhythm control. A tentative slot is being held for direct cardioversion on Wednesday, March 11 at 10:20 AM, with 8:50 AM arrival in the cardiac procedures unit; this slot is tentative and not yet confirmed with the patient or procedures unit. Marcus requests that the tentative Wednesday slot details be put in the chart. The scheduler will confirm whether that slot stays direct cardioversion or changes to a TEE-guided case. Dr. Patel has reviewed the labs and stated they are acceptable for outpatient cardioversion, satisfying the pending-labs condition; full medication history reconciliation remains part of the plan. Dr. Patel instructs that Marcus must not miss any apixaban doses at all between now and cardioversion. Pharmacist Klein confirms apixaban stays at 5 mg twice daily and Marcus must not stop or skip it on his own unless the cardiologist specifically says otherwise. The only routine periprocedural hold discussed is lisinopril on the morning of the procedure once the date is confirmed. Nurse Jamison will bring Marcus back first for his cardiology rhythm clinic visit, and Nina can be updated on arrival windows if Marcus keeps the logistics-only setting active. As of the latest update, Marcus is still being evaluated and no final arrival time has been set; Nina asked at the desk whether the timing changed, and Jamison told her only that Marcus is still being evaluated with no final arrival time set.

states.content: Nurse Jamison is reviewing Marcus Reed's medications exactly as he is taking them right now, to prepare an accurate current medication list. Marcus reported taking ibuprofen a couple of times last week for shoulder pain before remembering he probably should not with the blood thinner (apixaban). Dr. Patel has now instructed Marcus to stop ibuprofen and other NSAIDs and to use acetaminophen instead if needed, because NSAIDs raise bleeding risk with apixaban. Pharmacist Klein reinforced this: no ibuprofen or naproxen while Marcus is on apixaban. Marcus reported he has not missed any morning apixaban doses and no completely missed doses in the last three weeks as far as he remembers; he might have been a few hours late last Monday night when changing locations but still took that pill before bed. Nurse Jamison will document the Monday-night apixaban dose as possibly delayed but not skipped. Marcus does not drink energy drinks.
